what_it_does: Simulating how radio-frequency (RF) circuits behave under periodic signals — a technique called periodic small-signal analysis — is essential for designing wireless chips. One way to speed up such simulations is to reuse (recycle) a mathematical workspace called a Krylov subspace (a set of directions in a high-dimensional space that capture the most important dynamics of the circuit) from one simulation step to the next, rather than recomputing it from scratch. The problem is that this recycled workspace grows larger over time, consuming more and more memory. Restarting the simulation discards the recycled workspace and loses its benefit. This paper proposes a framework that selectively trims (truncates) the recycled subspace — keeping only its most useful parts using a method based on Floquet theory (which describes how periodic systems evolve) — so memory stays bounded while the speed-up from recycling is preserved.
